query: Earlier refractory high-entropy alloys illustrate persistent trade-offs: MoNbTaW and MoNbTaVW retained good yield strength from 600 to 1600 °C, with MoNbTaVW reaching 842 MPa at 1000 °C, but both had poor room-temperature fracture toughness and high density; HfNbTaTiZr showed room-temperature ductility above 50% and a yield strength of 929 MPa but only 295 MPa at 1000 °C; and as-cast HfMoTaTiZr achieved about 1600 MPa at room temperature and 855 MPa at elevated temperature but retained a density of 10.21 g cm−3. Given the constraint that density must be reduced without sacrificing the strong room- and high-temperature mechanical performance of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr, what single intervention should be tested? Provide a mechanistic hypothesis, predicted outcomes relative to the as-cast baseline, explicit temperature and loading boundary conditions, supporting evidence from the preceding RHEA results, and a controlled experiment with quantitative rejection criteria that could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Substitution of heavy elements with lighter ones in the as-cast HfMoTaTiZr alloy will reduce its density without sacrificing its strong room- and high-temperature mechanical performance.
generation.intervention: substitution of 20% of Hf with Sc
generation.conditions: room temperature to 1600 °C, yield strength loading
generation.structural_mediator: grain refinement and solid solution strengthening
generation.mechanism: reduction of density due to the lower atomic mass of Sc compared to Hf, while maintaining the solid solution strengthening effect
generation.predicted_outcome: a reduction in density of at least 5% (from 10.21 g cm−3 to 9.7 g cm−3) and a yield strength of at least 1500 MPa at room temperature and 800 MPa at 1000 °C
generation.baseline: as-cast HfMoTaTiZr with a density of 10.21 g cm−3, a yield strength of 1600 MPa at room temperature, and 855 MPa at elevated temperature
generation.boundary: temperature range from room temperature to 1600 °C, loading conditions up to yield strength
generation.uncertainty: the actual reduction in density and the resulting mechanical properties may vary depending on the specific substitution ratio and processing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: controlled substitution experiment with Sc substitution ratios of 0%, 10%, 20%, and 30%, followed by density and mechanical property measurements
measurements: yield strength at room temperature and 1000 °C
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if the density reduction is less than 3% or the yield strength at room temperature or 1000 °C is reduced by more than 10% compared to the as-cast HfMoTaTiZr, the hypothesis is falsified

goal.target: without sacrificing strong room- and high-temperature mechanical performance

limitation.current trade-off: poor room-temperature fracture toughness and high density or reduced high-temperature yield strength

precedents.problem: Revealing the role of Cr element on microstructure and properties of Co-Free FeCryNiAl0.8 High-Entropy Alloys
precedents.lever: phase-diagram calculations with microhardness, compression behavior measurements
precedents.outcome: The increment of Cr favors the regulation of the two-phase fraction and distribution, and the mechanical properties of the alloy in terms of strength and ductility at room temperature were optimized

precedents.outcome: Yield strengths approaching 1 GPa, persistent elongation up to 46% as well as the tensile strength of 1.3 GPa
